value: GFS-PY-T1 Governed Python File Size Coverage is CLOSED_PASS_BOUNDED at material commit fad16208 (dispatch/execution/closure base 75af9858). It upgraded governance/compat/check_python_automation_size.py from a flat soft/hard threshold to per-class thresholds (python_checker 700/1000, python_test 900/1200, python_library_helper 600/900, python_cli_orchestrator 500/800), added a touch rule (an excepted oversized file must not grow when modified unless approvedMaxLines is raised in the same governance change), a near-hard touched-file shrink/split rule, and a seedAuthorization bypass (a legacy exception is accepted only when its cited GC-018 baseline exists on disk); wired the guard into the local hook chain (pre-commit and pre-push) and the autorun pre-implementation phase; and seeded seven frozen legacy exceptions, each pointing at the GFS-PY split roadmap. No monolith was split in T0. The dispatch-quality decomposition is sequenced as held roadmap T1-T4 in docs/roadmaps/CVF_GOVERNED_PYTHON_FILE_SIZE_COVERAGE_ROADMAP_2026-06-25.md (T1 markdown/source-verification helpers, T2 lifecycle/status validators, T3 source-verification/token-collision validators, T4 orchestrator shell); each requires a fresh operator selection, GC-018, and source-verified work order, must be behavior-preserving, must not raise any seeded exception above its frozen line count, and must be proven by the existing dispatch-quality test suite. Enforcing non-governance Python (EXTENSIONS/, tools/, governance/skill-library/) is recorded as DEFERRED_RECORDED, not value-declined, and needs a separate coverage decision before any threshold is enforced there.
